hook.text: Your database has 10 terabytes. No single disk can hold it. No single CPU can query it fast enough.

buildup.text: Partitioning splits data across multiple nodes. Each node holds and processes a subset of the data.

discovery.text: Queries that hit one partition are fast. The node processes only its own data, not the entire dataset.

twist.text: Queries that span all partitions are slow. A scatter-gather across 100 nodes adds latency from the slowest one.

climax.text: Good partitioning ensures most queries hit one or few partitions. Bad partitioning defeats the purpose.

punchline.text: Split data so queries stay local to one partition.

quiz.question: Why is partitioning important?
options: No single machine can store or process the entire dataset
